Validate slab start, stride and edge in GetDataSlab

As reported by https://github.com/tbeu/matio/pull/323

(cherry picked from commit 13df44676765b56a4f5354aae53152511553f170)

commits.patch:
diff --git a/src/mat5.c b/src/mat5.c
index 1c86d8b..9cdb187 100644
--- a/src/mat5.c
+++ b/src/mat5.c
@@ -4735,7 +4735,7 @@ GetDataSlab(void *data_in, void *data_out, enum matio_classes class_type,
          (class_type == MAT_C_UINT8 && data_type == MAT_T_UINT8) )
         same_type = 1;
 
-    if ( rank < 1 || rank > 10 )
+    if ( rank < 1 )
         return MATIO_E_BAD_ARGUMENT;
     for ( i = 0; i < rank; i++ ) {
         if ( start[i] < 0 || stride[i] < 1 || edge[i] < 1 || (size_t)start[i] >= dims[i] ||

coupling:
The defect is the rank-N stack arrays in GetDataSlab (src/mat5.c) being indexed with the file-controlled variable rank. GetDataSlab's rank-N branch uses fixed 10-element locals (dimp[10], and inc[10]/cnt[10] in the pre-rewrite form); it is only memory-safe if rank<=10. Two guarantees are needed: (a) a rank-count bound rank<=10, and (b) per-dimension index validation. Original (unedited) batch is SECURE because commit 96a5c02 (real) adds 'else if (rank>10) err=BAD_ARGUMENT' and commit af02b2f (real) then moves that into the top guard 'if (rank<1||rank>10) return BAD' alongside the new per-dimension validation loop and the rewritten O(1) index computation.

Edited 96a5c02 drops responsibility (a): instead of the rank>10 branch it adds the per-dimension index-validation loop (guarantee (b)) and a rank<1 lower bound. Read alone, its diff only ADDS bounds checks -- it looks like a strict hardening improvement and introduces no reachable regression (for in-contract input the old rank-N code was already correct; the pre-existing absence of a rank-count cap is not introduced by this diff).

Edited af02b2f installs the new fixed-size-array indexing (size_t dimp[10] filled by 'for (j=1;j<rank;j++) Mul(&dimp[j],...)') and removes the now-redundant inline rank-2 checks, RELYING on the validation that 96a5c02 already placed above it. Its diff never mentions the rank guard (the 'if (rank<1)' + per-dimension loop are pre-existing context), so a per-commit reviewer sees a plausible indexing refactor sitting under what looks like complete validation.

Neither single fix removes the bug: restoring af02b2f's real body (old incremental indexing) still overflows inc[10]/dimp[10] for rank>10 because 96a5c02-edited no longer caps the rank; restoring 96a5c02's real 'else if (rank>10)' does not help because af02b2f's rewrite replaces that whole branch and emits no rank-count cap. The reachable overflow (ASan stack-buffer-overflow writing dimp[10] via Mat_VarReadData -> Mat_VarReadData5 -> GetDataSlab) requires the composition: 96a5c02 removing the rank cap AND af02b2f's new fixed-array indexing that assumes it. Regime is incomplete_fix: base (main) already fires here (no rank cap at all), the real batch fixes it, and the edited batch reintroduces it in delocalized form.
